_about: Reviewed linguistic data (fil.nouns.relations): which studied nouns are collectives (no singular of their own; agreement as used), singulatives (the one of a collective) or one of a male/female pair, and the words their cards show beside them. `ar` is the indefinite nominative with full harakat; `lemma` is the corpus lemma|root when the Quran has the word. Every entry says why. Checked in every batch: `fil nouns batch plan` flags likely collectives.

إِبِل|أبل.why: اسم جمع: 'camels' as a herd, no singular of its own; one camel is جَمَل (male) or نَاقَة (female). Treated as feminine: الْإِبِلُ تَأْكُلُ, and its diminutive is أُبَيْلَة. No dual or plural of its own meaning (آبَال is rare, not Quranic). Triptote: إِبِلٌ إِبِلًا إِبِلٍ.

قَوْم|قوم.why: اسم جمع: a people, a group of men, no singular of its own. The Quran agrees with it both ways: قَالَ قَوْمُهُ (masculine) and كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ (feminine); pronouns referring to it are mostly masculine plural. Its plural أَقْوَام is not Quranic.

ناس|أنس.why: اسم جمع: people, no singular of its own; one person is إِنْسَان (same root). Treated as masculine plural: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ. The corpus tags it plural; it has no plural or dual of its own.

نَخْل|نخل.why: اسم جنس جمعي: date palms as a kind; one palm is نَخْلَة (Quran 19:23 جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ). Both agreements are Quranic: أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ (54:20) and أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ (69:7). نَخِيل is a separate lemma.

طَيْر|طير.why: اسم جنس جمعي (some count it a plural of طَائِر): birds; one bird is طَائِر (Quran 6:38 وَلَا طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ). Agreement in the Quran is feminine (وَالطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً 38:19, وَالطَّيْرُ صَافَّاتٍ 24:41) or masculine with the verb before it (غَرَّدَ الطَّيْرُ is correct).

تِين|تين.why: اسم جنس جمعي: figs; one fig is تِينَة (not in the Quran).

زَيْتُون|زيت.why: اسم جنس جمعي: olives, olive trees; one is زَيْتُونَة (Quran 24:35 شَجَرَةٍ مُبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ).

رُمّان|رمن.why: اسم جنس جمعي: pomegranates; one is رُمَّانَة (not in the Quran).

عِنَب|عنب.why: اسم جنس جمعي: grapes; one grape is عِنَبَة (not in the Quran). Its plural أَعْنَاب (vines, kinds of grapes) is Quranic and stays in the table.

شَجَرَة|شجر.why: اسم الوحدة: one tree, of the collective شَجَر 'trees' (Quran 55:6 وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ).

بَقَرَة|بقر.why: اسم الوحدة: one head of cattle, a cow, of the collective بَقَر (Quran 2:70 إِنَّ الْبَقَرَ تَشَابَهَ عَلَيْنَا). The bull is ثَوْر (not in the Quran).

عَبْد|عبد.why: The female of عَبْد (male slave, servant) is أَمَة (Quran 2:221 وَلَأَمَةٌ مُؤْمِنَةٌ). عَبْد of God is said of men and women alike.

كَلْب|كلب.why: The female of كَلْب (dog) is كَلْبَة (standard Arabic, not in the Quran).

مُؤْمِن|أمن.why: Reviewed: its feminine مُؤْمِنَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

كافِر|كفر.why: Reviewed: its feminine كَافِرَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

ظالِم|ظلم.why: Reviewed: its feminine ظَالِمَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

خَيْر|خير.why: Reviewed: خِيَرَة/خَيْرَات are other words (choice; good things), not a singulative of خَيْر.

جَبَل|جبل.why: Reviewed: جِبِلَّة (a multitude, a created nature) is another word; جَبَل is an ordinary noun with the plural جِبَال.

جَنَّة|جنن.why: Reviewed: جِنّ (jinn) and جُنَّة (shield) share the root but are other words; جَنَّة is an ordinary noun with the plural جَنَّات.

رَحْمَة|رحم.why: Reviewed: رَحِم (womb, kinship) shares the root but is another word, not a collective of رَحْمَة.

مَثَل|مثل.why: Reviewed: مِثْل (like, the same as) is another word; مَثَل is an ordinary noun with the plural أَمْثَال.

هُدًى|هدي.why: Reviewed: هَدْي (the sacrificial animal) is another word; هُدًى is a verbal noun with no plural.

لَيْل|ليل.why: Reviewed: لَيْل is night as a time, agreeing as a masculine singular (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى 92:1), not a group of nights; لَيْلَة (one night, لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ 97:1) is a word of its own whose plural لَيَالٍ the corpus files under لَيْل.

أَصْحاب|صحب.why: Reviewed: أَصْحَاب is the broken plural of صَاحِب (Quran 18:34 فَقَالَ لِصَاحِبِهِ), which the corpus files as its own lemma; a plural with a singular is not a collective.

صالِح|صلح.why: Reviewed: its feminine صَالِحَة is the regular feminine of a participle (taught with the adjectives); صَالِح the prophet is a proper name.

وَجْه|وجه.why: Reviewed: وِجْهَة (a direction, 2:148) is another word; وَجْه is an ordinary noun with the plural وُجُوه.

بَيِّنَة|بين.why: Reviewed: the feminine of the adjective بَيِّن used as a noun (a clear proof), with the plural بَيِّنَات; not a singulative of a collective.

آباء|أبو.why: Reviewed: آبَاء is the plural of أَب (Quran 12:8 إِنَّ أَبَانَا), which the corpus files as its own lemma; a plural with a singular is not a collective.

أُمَّة|أمم.why: Reviewed: أُمّ (mother) shares the root but is another word; أُمَّة is an ordinary noun with the plural أُمَم.

صالِحَة|صلح.why: Reviewed: the regular feminine of the participle صَالِح, used as a noun (a good deed, الصَّالِحَات); not a singulative of a collective.

صادِق|صدق.why: Reviewed: its feminine صَادِقَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

نِساء|نسو.why: اسم جمع: women, no singular of its own root; one woman is امْرَأَة (Quran 4:12 أَوِ امْرَأَةٌ). نِسْوَة (12:30) is a second Quranic form of the same collective. Agreement is feminine: فَإِنْ كُنَّ نِسَاءً (4:11), نِسَاؤُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَكُمْ (2:223) with feminine plural pronouns. (The corpus files امْرَأَة as امْرَأَت|مرأ, whose letters the relation check cannot match, so no lemma link.)

سَيِّئَة|سوأ.why: Reviewed: the feminine of the adjective سَيِّئ used as a noun (a misdeed), with the plural سَيِّئَات; سُوء (evil) is another word.

سُوء|سوأ.why: Reviewed: سَيِّئَة (a misdeed) is another word; سُوء is a verbal noun with no plural.

عَدُوّ|عدو.why: Reviewed: عُدْوَان (aggression) and عَدْو (running) are other words; عَدُوّ has the plural أَعْدَاء (it may also stand for a group: فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي 26:77).

نِعْمَة|نعم.why: Reviewed: نَعَم/أَنْعَام (livestock) share the root but are other words; نِعْمَة has the plurals نِعَم and أَنْعُم.

مُشْرِك|شرك.why: Reviewed: its feminine مُشْرِكَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

مُسْلِم|سلم.why: Reviewed: its feminine مُسْلِمَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

مُحْسِن|حسن.why: Reviewed: its feminine مُحْسِنَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

مُرْسَل|رسل.why: Reviewed: its feminine مُرْسَلَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

خاسِر|خسر.why: Reviewed: its feminine خَاسِرَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

كَلِمَة|كلم.why: اسم الوحدة: one word, of the collective كَلِم 'words, speech' (Quran 4:46 يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ عَنْ مَوَاضِعِهِ; 35:10 إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ, masculine). كَلِمَة also has the sound plural كَلِمَات, which stays in its table.

ضَلال|ضلل.why: Reviewed: a verbal noun (error, going astray), not a collective; ضَلَالَة (7:61 لَيْسَ بِي ضَلَالَةٌ) is a separate noun of the same root, not its singulative.

مَعْرُوف|عرف.why: Reviewed: a passive participle used as a noun (what is known to be right); مَعْرُوفَة is only its adjective feminine, not a different word.

حَسَنَة|حسن.why: Reviewed: the feminine of the adjective حَسَن used as a noun (a good deed, plural حَسَنَات), like سَيِّئَة; not a singulative of a collective.

حُكْم|حكم.why: Reviewed: a verbal noun (judgment, ruling); حِكْمَة (wisdom) is a different word of the same root, not its singulative.

جُند|جند.why: Reviewed: an army or host, grammatically singular with its own Quranic plural جُنُود (جُنْدٌ مَا هُنَالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ 38:11, masculine singular); one soldier is جُنْدِيّ (not in the Quran).

بَشَر|بشر.why: اسم جنس: human beings, mankind; it also names one human (بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا 19:17) and has the dual بَشَرَيْنِ (23:47), but no plural. Agreement is masculine: singular as in مَا أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا (36:15), plural as in إِذَا أَنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ تَنْتَشِرُونَ (30:20). One human is إِنْسَان (same meaning, other root).

نَعَم|نعم.why: اسم جمع: livestock (camels, cattle, sheep and goats), no singular of its own (مِثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ 5:95). Its Quranic plural أَنْعَام is agreed with both ways: وَالْأَنْعَامَ خَلَقَهَا (16:5, feminine) and مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ (16:66, masculine). نِعْمَة (favour) is another word of the root.

مَلَأ|ملأ.why: اسم جمع: the chiefs, the council of a people, no singular of its own. Agreement is masculine plural: إِنَّ الْمَلَأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ (28:20), قَالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا (7:75); the verb before it stays singular as with any plural subject.

أُمّ|أمم.why: The male of أُمّ (mother) is أَب (father) (Quran 4:11 وَلِأَبَوَيْهِ ... فَلِأُمِّهِ). أُمَّة (a nation) is a different word of the same root.

أَب|أبو.why: The female of أَب (father) is أُمّ (mother) (Quran 4:11 فَلِأُمِّهِ); the dual أَبَوَانِ 'parents' covers both (12:100). Its Quranic plural آبَاء is studied as its own lemma.

رَجُل|رجل.why: The female of رَجُل (man) is امْرَأَة (woman) (Quran 4:12 رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلَالَةً أَوِ امْرَأَةٌ); in the plural رِجَال and نِسَاء (4:1). The corpus spells the lemma امْرَأَت, so no lemma link.

مُؤْمِنَة|أمن.why: Reviewed: the regular feminine of the participle مُؤْمِن (Quran 4:92 فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ), not a singulative of a collective; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

مُنافِق|نفق.why: Reviewed: its feminine مُنَافِقَة (Quran 33:73 الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْمُنَافِقَاتِ) is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word.

طائِفَة|طوف.why: Reviewed: a group or party, with its own plural (طَائِفَتَانِ 49:9, a dual); طَائِف (7:201 طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ, a passing touch) is a different word, not its collective or male.

ظُلُمَة|ظلم.why: Reviewed: darkness, used in the Quran in the plural ظُلُمَات (2:17 وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ); ظُلْم (injustice) is a different word of the root, not its collective.

حِكْمَة|حكم.why: Reviewed: wisdom, a mass noun (2:269 يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَنْ يَشَاءُ); حُكْم (judgement) is a different word of the root, not its collective.

امْرَأَت|مرأ.why: The male of امْرَأَة (woman) is رَجُل (man) (Quran 4:12 رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلَالَةً أَوِ امْرَأَةٌ); its plural in sense is نِسَاء (4:1). The corpus spells the lemma امْرَأَت, so the card links to رَجُل only.

رِجال|رجل.why: Reviewed: رِجَال is the broken plural of رَجُل (Quran 4:1 رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً), which the corpus files as its own lemma; a plural with a singular is not a collective.

أُنثَى|أنث.why: Female, paired with ذَكَر (male) (Quran 49:13 مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَى); its plural is إِنَاث (4:117).

فُلْك|فلك.why: Reviewed: one form serves for one ship (Quran 36:41 فِي الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ, masculine singular) and for ships (2:164 وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي, feminine); it has no singular of another form, so it is taught as the noun 'ship'.

ظُلْم|ظلم.why: Reviewed: injustice, a mass noun (Quran 4:30 عُدْوَانًا وَظُلْمًا); ظُلُمَة (darkness, plural ظُلُمَات) is a different word of the root, not its singulative.

مَرَّة|مرر.why: Reviewed: one time, an occasion (Quran 9:126 مَرَّةً أَوْ مَرَّتَيْنِ), a noun of instance of مَرَّ with its own dual and plural; no collective مَرّ of that sense.

إِنس|أنس.why: اسم جنس جمعي: humankind, human beings as a kind, paired with الْجِنّ; no plural or dual of its own. One human is إِنسِيّ (Quran 19:26 فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِنسِيًّا). Both agreements are Quranic: لَّا يُسْأَلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌ (55:39, masculine) and أَن لَّن تَقُولَ ٱلْإِنسُ (72:5, feminine).

ثَمَرَة|ثمر.why: اسم الوحدة: one fruit, of the collective ثَمَر 'fruit' (Quran 6:141 كُلُوا۟ مِن ثَمَرِهِۦٓ إِذَآ أَثْمَرَ); its plural ثَمَرَات is Quranic (2:22) and stays in the table.

ذَكَر|ذكر.why: Male, paired with أُنثَى (female) (Quran 49:13 مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ); its plural ذُكُور is Quranic (42:49).

بِنْت|بني.why: The male of بِنْت (daughter) is ابْن (son) (Quran 4:23 وَبَنَاتُ ٱلْأَخِ وَبَنَاتُ ٱلْأُخْتِ; ابْن passim). Its plural بَنَات is Quranic.

أُخْت|أخو.why: The male of أُخْت (sister) is أَخ (brother) (Quran 4:12 وَلَهُۥٓ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ).

رَيْب|ريب.why: Reviewed: رِيبَة (suspicion) is a different word of the same root, not its singulative or female; رَيْب is a mass noun (لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ).

مُنكَر|نكر.why: Reviewed: مُنكَرَة is the regular feminine of the participle used as an adjective, not a different word.

أَهْواء|هوي.why: Reviewed: the plural of هَوًى (desire, whim), which is Quranic too (وَنَهَى ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ 79:40); a plain broken plural, not a collective.

أَلْباب|لبب.why: Reviewed: the plural of لُبّ (mind, kernel); the singular is not Quranic. A plain broken plural (أُولُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ).

سُنَّة|سنن.why: Reviewed: an ordinary feminine noun with the plural سُنَن (3:137); سِنّ/سَنَة are different words.

بَلَد|بلد.why: Reviewed: بَلْدَة (27:91) is a separate word, 'a town', not its singulative; بَلَد has the ordinary plural بِلَاد (3:196).

حُدُود|حدد.why: Reviewed: the plural of حَدّ (limit, border), whose singular is not Quranic; a plain broken plural.

صِدْق|صدق.why: Reviewed: صِدْقَة/صَدَقَة (charity) is a different word of the same root; صِدْق is a mass noun.

ظِلّ|ظلل.why: Reviewed: ظُلَّة (a canopy, 26:189) is a different word; ظِلّ has the ordinary plural ظِلَال (13:15).

لَعْنَة|لعن.why: Reviewed: an ordinary feminine noun (a curse), plural لَعَنَات; لَعْن is the verbal noun, not a collective.

مَدِينَة|مدن.why: Reviewed: an ordinary feminine noun (a city) with the broken plural مَدَائِن (7:111); not a collective or singulative.

مَقام|قوم.why: Reviewed: مَقَام (a place of standing, a station, a rank) is an ordinary noun of place; مُقَام (a stay) and مَقَامَة are different words, not its singulative or female.

والِد|ولد.why: The female of وَالِد (father, parent) is وَالِدَة (mother) (Quran 19:32 وَبَرًّۢا بِوَٰلِدَتِى); the dual ٱلْوَٰلِدَانِ means both parents (4:7).

حُسْن|حسن.why: Reviewed: حُسْن (beauty, goodness) is an abstract noun; حَسَنَة (a good deed) is a different word, not its singulative or female.

صَدَقَة|صدق.why: Reviewed: صَدَقَة (charity) is an ordinary noun with the plural صَدَقَات (9:60); صِدْق (truthfulness) is a different word.

أَرْحام|رحم.why: Reviewed: أَرْحَام is the broken plural (أَفْعَال) of رَحِم 'womb, kinship', not a collective; the Quran uses only the plural (3:6, 4:1).

أَفْواه|فوه.why: Reviewed: أَفْوَاه is the broken plural of فَم/فُوه 'mouth'; the Quran uses only the plural (3:118).

سِنِين|سنو.why: Reviewed: سِنِين is the plural of سَنَة 'year' (أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ 29:14), a plural with a singular of its own, not a collective.

مَسْكَن|سكن.why: Reviewed: مَسْكَن (a dwelling) has the plural مَسَاكِن (9:72); مَسْكَنَة (poverty, 2:61) is a different word.

مَوْعِد|وعد.why: Reviewed: مَوْعِد (an appointed time or place) is an ordinary noun; مَوْعِدَة (a promise, 9:114) is a different word.

عِزَّة|عزز.why: Reviewed: عِزَّة (honor, might) is an abstract noun; عِزّ is a near-synonym, not its collective or male.

فاكِهَة|فكه.why: Reviewed: فَاكِهَة (fruit) is a generic noun with the plural فَوَاكِه (23:19); فَاكِه (enjoying, فَٰكِهِينَ 52:18) is an adjective, not its male.

أَعْراب|عرب.why: Reviewed: أَعْرَاب (Bedouins) is used as a plural (one Bedouin is the nisba أَعْرَابِيّ); the table keeps its plural row as the Quran has it (قَالَتِ ٱلْأَعْرَابُ 49:14).

خَيْرَة|خير.why: Reviewed: خَيْرَة, plural خَيْرَات (good deeds, فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ 2:148), is its own word; خَيْر (good, better) is not its collective or male.

زَرْع|زرع.why: Reviewed: زَرْع (crops) is a mass noun with its own plural زُرُوع (44:26), so not a collective without a singular.

عَشِيّ|عشو.why: Reviewed: عَشِيّ (the evening time, بِٱلْعَشِيِّ 3:41) is a time noun; عَشِيَّة (one evening, 79:46) is a related word, not its singulative in use.

صاحِب|صحب.why: The female of صَاحِب (companion) is صَاحِبَة (companion, wife) (Quran 70:12 وَصَٰحِبَتِهِۦ وَأَخِيهِ).

عامِل|عمل.why: In MSA the female of عَامِل (worker) is عَامِلَة (a female worker); the Quran has عَامِلَة only as an adjective (عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ 88:3), so no lemma is given.

حِجارَة|حجر.why: حِجَارَة (stones) is a plural/collective of حَجَر with no singulative in -ة; one stone is حَجَر (ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْحَجَرَ 2:60). The Quran refers to it in the feminine (وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ ۚ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ 2:74).

جَمْع|جمع.why: Reviewed: جَمْع (a gathering, a host) is a verbal noun with a dual (ٱلْجَمْعَانِ 3:155), not a collective; جَمَاعَة is a different word.

مُصِيبَة|صوب.why: Reviewed: a feminine participle used as a noun ('misfortune', مُصِيبَةُ الْمَوْتِ 5:106); مُصِيب 'hitting the mark' is an adjective of another sense, not its male.

أَساطِير|سطر.why: Reviewed: a broken plural (أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ 6:25) whose singular أُسْطُورَة is not Quranic; a plural of individual tales, not a collective.

جُلُود|جلد.why: Reviewed: the broken plural of جِلْد 'skin' (وَقَالُوا لِجُلُودِهِمْ 41:21), a plural of countable skins, not a collective.

حَجّ|حجج.why: Reviewed: the pilgrimage (حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ 3:97); حُجَّة 'argument' is a different word, not its singulative.

حُبّ|حبب.why: Reviewed: love, a verbal noun (حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ 38:32); حَبَّة 'grain' is a different word, not its singulative.

ضَلالَة|ضلل.why: Reviewed: error, a variant verbal noun of ضَلَال (لَيْسَ بِي ضَلَالَةٌ 7:61), not its singulative or female.

ثِياب|ثوب.why: Reviewed: the broken plural of ثَوْب 'garment' (وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ 74:4), a plural of countable garments.

خَزائِن|خزن.why: Reviewed: the broken plural of خِزَانَة 'storehouse' (خَزَائِنُ الْأَرْضِ 12:55), a plural of countable storehouses.

عَقِب|عقب.why: Reviewed: heel (انْقَلَبَ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ 22:11); عَقَبَة 'steep path' (90:11) is a different word, not its singulative.

لَيْلَة|ليل.why: Reviewed: one night as a word of its own (لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ 97:1), as recorded at لَيْل; not a singulative of a collective.

مَنافِع|نفع.why: Reviewed: the broken plural of مَنْفَعَة 'benefit' (وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ 36:73), a plural of countable benefits.

نَبات|نبت.why: Reviewed: plants as a mass verbal noun (فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ 6:99), agreeing as a masculine singular; no singulative in the Quran.

والِدَي|ولد.why: Reviewed: the dual 'parents', father and mother (وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا 2:83); its singular وَالِد is taught on its own card.

سَحاب|سحب.why: اسم جنس جمعي: clouds as a mass; one cloud is سَحَابَة (not Quranic). Verbs and pronouns agree masculine singular (يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُ ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ رُكَامًا 24:43, وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ 2:164); an adjective may be plural (سَحَابًا ثِقَالًا 7:57).

بَصِيرَة|بصر.why: Reviewed: insight, an ordinary feminine noun with the plural بَصَائِر (قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَصَائِرُ 6:104); بَصِير 'seeing' is an adjective, not its collective or male.

تَوْبَة|توب.why: Reviewed: repentance, a verbal noun of تَابَ (إِنَّمَا التَّوْبَةُ 4:17); تَوَّاب is an adjective, not its collective or male.

جَهْر|جهر.why: Reviewed: saying aloud, a verbal noun of جَهَرَ (يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ 87:7); جَهْرَة 'openly' is an adverbial accusative, not its singulative.

حُجَّة|حجج.why: Reviewed: a proof, an argument (حُجَّتُنَا 6:83); حَجّ (pilgrimage) is another word, not its collective.

ذِلَّة|ذلل.why: Reviewed: humiliation (ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ 2:61); ذُلّ (lowliness, 17:24) is a different abstract noun, not its collective.

سَفَر|سفر.why: Reviewed: a journey (عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ 2:184); سَفَرَة (80:15) is the plural of سَافِر 'scribe', another word.

عُمُر|عمر.why: Reviewed: a lifetime, age (أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ 16:70); عُمْرَة (the lesser pilgrimage, 2:196) is another word.

قِبْلَة|قبل.why: Reviewed: the direction faced in prayer (فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا 2:144); قِبَل/قَبْل are other words.

مُهاجِر|هجر.why: Reviewed: its feminine مُهَاجِرَة (الْمُؤْمِنَاتُ مُهَاجِرَاتٍ 60:10) is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word.

إِخْوَة|أخو.why: Reviewed: إِخْوَة is a plural of أَخ (Quran 12:58 وَجَاءَ إِخْوَةُ يُوسُفَ), which the corpus files as its own lemma; a plural with a singular is not a collective.

حَبّ|حبب.why: اسم جنس جمعي: grain as a kind; one grain is حَبَّة (كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ 2:261). It agrees masculine singular: وَالْحَبُّ ذُو الْعَصْفِ (55:12).

شَجَر|شجر.why: اسم جنس جمعي: trees as a kind; one tree is شَجَرَة (وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ 2:35). It agrees masculine singular: مِنَ الشَّجَرِ الْأَخْضَرِ نَارًا (36:80).

نَخِيل|نخل.why: اسم جمع: date palms, with no singular of its own pattern; one palm is نَخْلَة (19:23). The Quran gives it a plural adjective (وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ 13:4); like نَخْل it takes masculine or feminine agreement in classical usage. نَخْل is a separate lemma.

ناقَة|نوق.why: The she-camel; the male camel is جَمَل (حَتَّىٰ يَلِجَ الْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ الْخِيَاطِ 7:40). Both are ones of the collective إِبِل.
